why: An INPUT, not a run artifact -- the same role docs/live-test-results/arch-arms-
sampling.json plays for the four-arm harness, and deliberately a SECOND file
rather than a section inside that one. arch_arms.load_config validates over its
own ARM_ORDER (E/W/M/H); adding B0/B1 cells there would be read by nothing and
would put two tasks' hands on one file. This table is the hive's, and
examples/arch_hive.py defines no fallback for any cell in it: a missing cell
raises ConfigError naming the arm and the role, asserted structurally over the
module's own AST so a default cannot be reintroduced quietly.
Model identities live here for arch_arms' reason, unchanged: the cortex 'model'
is null on purpose, resolved from the environment or recorded ABSENT -- never
substituted with a predecessor.
NULL DELIBERATELY, matching arch-arms-sampling.json. The cortex is the only
mind that holds a loop in either hive tier and the only one that finishes.
Dialled DIRECTLY at Thor through examples/worker_seam.py -- spec decision
c42: B1's scoped calls are plain concurrent scoped calls on the worker_seam
path the throughput probe already measured, NOT fan-out unit dispatch. Only
units that hold turns need turn budgets partitioned, and a hive worker holds
no turn at all.
Constant in both tiers and NOT dialled by them -- recorded and hashed so a
senses difference cannot confound the B0/B1 contrast invisibly.
What 'thinking: on' puts on the wire, stated rather than assumed. A mode with
no entry here is a config error, never a silent no-op.
Per role per arm. The cortex cell matches arch-arms-sampling.json exactly so
the hive tiers are comparable with E/W/M/H rather than confounded by sampling.
The worker cell does NOT: a scoped answer is tens of tokens, thinking is off,
and max_tokens is small on purpose -- a hive call that needed a 16000-token
budget would not be a scoped question. The value is an instrument setting the
t8 overhead probe and the t9 pre-registration may amend; it is here so that
amendment is an edit to a cited file, not to code.
max_steps is the cortex's own drive budget. worker_max_steps is 0 in BOTH
tiers and that is the arm's whole claim: a hive worker never drives, so there
is no turn budget to grant it. spawn_allowance is 0 for the same reason -- the
hive passes no subagent seam at all, so nothing can be spawned even by
accident. max_scoped_calls bounds the number of scoped calls one drive may
dispatch, in total, across every transform invocation; it is the step-count
bound the structural termination test reads.
The tier table. B0 and B1 differ in exactly ONE field -- answerer -- which is
what makes B0 a control for B1 rather than a different experiment: identical
cortex surface, identical questions, identical grain vocabulary, and the only
variable is whether a scoped answer comes from a declared code rule or from a
bounded worker call.
B2 has NO entry here on purpose. B2 is an open goal with the worker holding
control, which is arm M in examples/arch_arms.py -- already built, already
dialable. Declaring it here would be a second implementation of a shipped arm.
RIGID. Zero worker model calls at play time: every scoped answer comes from
the 'first' code policy, which answers the first member of the declared
space. Deliberately a WEAK baseline and named as one -- it is the floor a
scoped tier must beat, never a serious solver. max_concurrency 1 because
there is nothing to overlap: a code answer costs no round trip.
SCOPED. N small worker calls, concurrent, each a typed question with an
enumerable answer space; the harness keeps control flow throughout.
max_concurrency 8 is measured saturation (docs/live-test-results/worker-
throughput.md): 8 to 14 buys +5.5% aggregate for +75% concurrent load, and
the advertised x14 is a KV-pool ceiling lobes has relabelled. code_policy is
carried even though B1 does not use it, so a degraded run that has to fall
back names the rule it fell back to instead of inventing one.
SCOPE SIZE IS THE INDEPENDENT VARIABLE (frame assumption: swept, not toggled).
It lives here as a named table so the t9 sweep varies a cited config value
rather than editing a prompt. items_per_call is the whole of it: how many
things ride in one scoped call, which sets both the number of calls and the
amount of context each one re-pays. Task t8 measures that per-call prefill
cost before t9 fixes the sweep's granularity -- no grain here is claimed to be
the right one, they are the rungs the sweep may dial.

unit.why: one thing per call -- the finest grain, the most calls, the most prefill

batch4.why: coarse enough that a single refusal costs four answers -- the acceptance risk

batch8.why: the coarse end: one call at measured saturation width, prefill paid once

why: The wait deadline for one concurrent scoped batch. Derived, not chosen: the
frame's rule is REQUEST_TIMEOUT >= max_tokens / slowest measured rate, and a
hive batch holds ONE turn per call (never a drive), so the bound is the
per-turn bound with no turn-budget multiplier -- unlike the fan-out deadline,
which bounds a whole unit drive.
256 tokens / 21.5 tok/s = 11.9s; the value below carries a wide margin for
queueing on a --max-num-seqs=2 server rather than sitting near the bound. Task
t2 owns the CI test that recomputes this class of constant; this cell exists
so the hive's deadline is a cited config value when t2 walks it, never a
literal in examples/arch_hive.py.
PROVISIONAL and named as such -- task t9's pre-registration is the authority on
the sweep, the outcome metric and the stop rule. It lives here as data so t9
can pin or amend it without a code change.
call_acceptance_refutes_at_rate is the number the frame names by hand: issue
#33 measured 74% of workspace-arm calls refused on a shape error, and the
delegate-to-authored-artifacts claim predicts that class disappears when the
cortex authors the schema. A B tier at that rate is published as REFUTING the
claim, by name, not smoothed over.
